outcome: Long-term neurological outcomes (at 7 years of age)
cohort: The study included 49 women and their children born via forceps delivery at a single clinic in Serbia between January 2012 and December 2016.
finding: The study found that 16.3% of newborns had pathological neurological status and 6.4% had long-term adverse neurological outcomes at 7 years of age, though these were generally mild disorders and associations with perinatal factors like Apgar score and perinatal asphyxia were unlikely to be related to the mode of delivery.
mod_finding: The study suggests the safety of forceps delivery regarding children's neurological outcomes at 7 years of age.
